summary: 30-foot pole L-4 tower on Sweetgrass Butte in Okanogan County, built 1933 with a 1932 staffed lookout before it; sold for removal in 1967. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Sold to a local resident for removal in 1967; the cab smashed to the ground during removal

access.note: No source read says whether the public may visit the site. A 1936 article describes a road route to it; a 1973 article says it still served as an emergency lookout

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb according to the sources read; none describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on November 23, 2012
George Storms began observing in mid-July 1932; Willhite says the site was still a camp at the time, before the tower was built
Register, firelookout.com and Willhite give 1933 for the 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab
Aircraft Warning Service used the lookout to watch for enemy aircraft; the service built sleeping quarters and reconditioned it. Active March 16, 1942 to July 1, 1943
Dan Noble listed as known lookout personnel
Mike Lynch listed as known lookout personnel
Keith Casey listed as known lookout personnel
Ward Shafer, lookout guard, reported 240 visitors that summer
Herald-Reporter (1973, quoted by Willhite) says permanent use was discontinued in the mid-1960s; 1965 stands for the mid-1960s
Tower sold to a local resident for removal; the cab smashed to the ground when it was being removed by crane
Herald-Reporter says the site still served as an emergency lookout during lightning storms and high fire danger weather

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and Willhite all give 1933 for the tower. Willhite also says a lookout was staffed in 1932 when the site was still a camp, so the story reports the 1932 staffing without treating it as the build date.

The tower was sold for removal in 1967, yet a 1973 article quoted by Willhite says the site still served as an emergency lookout. The sources do not say what served that role after the tower was gone, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Only three pages describe this tower in the sources read, and none describes the site today. Registration date November 23, 2012 on the FFLOS page matches the brief. The AllTrails route page returned HTTP 403, and NHLR had no page at the guessed URL, so neither was used. Two web searches surfaced only route listings and an unrelated fire page, none about the lookout site, so nothing from them is cited. The Willhite AWS document names the station in the Chelan National Forest while FFLOS lists Okanogan National Forest today; the story does not use either name for the agency. Willhite's 1965 and 1934 photo captions have no image URLs read, so no photos were added. Access is unknown; it is not recorded as closed because no source says so. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1932 lookout is the observer George Storms, not a structure, and the story now says so. The 1936 article is by the Brewster Herald and the 1973 item is from the Herald-Reporter, both as quoted by Willhite. No source says what served the emergency-lookout role after the 1967 removal.
